DI48 is the ICD-10 diagnosis code for atrial fibrillation. It serves as the central diagnostic cornerstone for the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (AFDK), defining both the incident and prevalent patient populations used in the database's epidemiological and clinical analyses [^src1]. 

The code is utilized across multiple national registries to identify patients. Specifically, patients with atrial fibrillation are defined as those registered in the [[landspatientregisteret|Landspatientregisteret]] and in the practice systems of private practicing cardiologists with the ICD-10 diagnosis DI48, including all subcodes [^src2]. In the context of the [[landspatientregisteret|Landspatientregisteret]], the code is captured whether it is recorded as a primary (action) or secondary diagnosis [^src4]. 

Methodologically, DI48 is critical for delineating the incident population, which comprises all patients receiving an initial diagnosis of atrial fibrillation (DI48 and subcodes) within the most recent 10 years of the reporting period [^src1]. This precise coding allows the AFDK to track clinical quality indicators—such as the occurrence of heart failure within one year of a new atrial fibrillation diagnosis—and to benchmark cardiovascular healthcare quality across Denmark's five regions [^src3].
